standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice asking for help. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Without being told exactly what to do, the learner identifies a real (or provided) situation where they're genuinely stuck on something, decides who's the right person to ask, and makes a specific request for help rather than a vague complaint.
safetyNotes: The situation and the person asked stay within the learner's normal household or trusted circle; no disclosure of private family details is required.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real stuck situation comes up, the learner instead responds to a provided scenario describing someone who's stuck, choosing the right person to ask and writing the specific request they would make in that situation.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Rate your confidence in asking for help well (very / somewhat / not yet), cite today's specific request as evidence, and choose: ready to try a harder ask, ready to review this again, or need a different explanation.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Choosing the right person to ask: Asks a plausible person with a stated reason. | Request specificity: Request names the specific problem. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Help someone else who's stuck on something, using the same specific-request skill in reverse — noticing what kind of help they actually need.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice asking for help. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: none required
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: asking for help worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Without being told exactly what to do, the learner identifies a real (or provided) situation where they're genuinely stuck on something, decides who's the right person to ask, and makes a specific request for help rather than a vague complaint.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact asking for help decision or action.
Model move 2: Quickly recall: name one recent time you were stuck on something and didn't ask for help.
Model move 3: Identify a real situation where you're stuck right now, choose the right person to ask, and make a specific help request.
Model check: Choosing the right person to ask: Asks a plausible person with a stated reason. | Request specificity: Request names the specific problem.

resources.title: asking for help action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for asking for help.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: asking for help coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Without being told exactly what to do, the learner identifies a real (or provided) situation where they're genuinely stuck on something, decides who's the right person to ask, and makes a specific request for help rather than a vague complaint.
Coach direction: Quickly recall: name one recent time you were stuck on something and didn't ask for help.
Learner prompt: Describe that time.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking for help complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Identify a real situation where you're stuck right now, choose the right person to ask, and make a specific help request.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Describe the situation, who you asked, and exactly what you asked for.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My request named the specific problem, not just 'I need help.'

Equal-access rule: If no real stuck situation comes up, the learner instead responds to a provided scenario describing someone who's stuck, choosing the right person to ask and writing the specific request they would make in that situation.

resources.title: asking for help minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Rate your confidence in asking for help well (very / somewhat / not yet), cite today's specific request as evidence, and choose: ready to try a harder ask, ready to review this again, or need a different explanation.
Success checks: Choosing the right person to ask: Asks a plausible person with a stated reason. | Request specificity: Request names the specific problem.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking for help supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking for help condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.
Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Choosing the right person to ask: Asks a plausible person with a stated reason. | Request specificity: Request names the specific problem..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: Without being told exactly what to do, the learner identifies a real (or provided) situation where they're genuinely stuck on something, decides who's the right person to ask, and makes a specific request for help rather than a vague complaint.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.

realRoute.title: asking for help — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Identify a real situation where you're stuck right now, choose the right person to ask, and make a specific help request.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: asking for help — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Choosing the right person to ask: Asks a plausible person with a stated reason. | Request specificity: Request names the specific problem.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
